veteran_rest_day_tell_on_production.classification_evidence: Assigned-window (2020-2021, rotation family veteran_rest_day_tell_on_production) week-blocked interval [-5.765,+0.222] crosses zero: not a resolved wrong sign. Trait reliability (team rest-tag rate, odd vs even season halves, 32 teams) Pearson r=0.5633 95%% [0.285,0.768] excludes zero: rules out no_split_half_reliability. No positive-control-sized bound attempted at this effect size. Neither admissible closing ground applies.
veteran_rest_day_tell_on_production.description: Value-weighted count of flagged 30+ veteran starters (Wednesday DNP/rest or not-injury-related reason text, cleared to practice later that week) stacked as a FADE overlay on production's opener probability-rule pick.
veteran_rest_day_tell_on_production.notes: docs/veteran_rest_day_tell.md; scripts/veteran_rest_day_tell.py. Full 2020-2025 opener archive (1537 games, descriptive only, NOT the recorded confirmation cell): -2.7944 pts, 95%% [-4.573,-1.002], P+ 0.00105. Outcome comparison (2021-2025, 1022 flagged player-weeks): raw same-week snap share is HIGHER for flagged veterans than the general 30+ population (selection: only high-usage starters get rest days), but once matched to trailing-starter status only (n=790 flagged vs 8381 control), flagged veterans show a SMALLER production drop from their own trailing baseline (-0.0154 vs -0.0273) and a LOWER 4-week missed-game rate (0.195 vs 0.251) than matched non-flagged starters, both directions consistent across odd (2021/23/25) and even (2022/24) season halves -- pointing away from the predeclared hidden-decline mechanism. Birth dates: 100%% coverage via nflreadpy.load_players() (32 null league-wide), unlike the prior NFL.com-sourced screen (docs/injury_trajectory_leads.md) which had zero coverage.
veteran_rest_day_tell_on_production.plain_summary: When a team rests a 30+ veteran on Wednesday for a non-injury reason and he returns to practice, betting against that team lost a little accuracy rather than gaining it (39 of 466 games would have flipped); not enough games yet to be sure either way.
